findings.problem: All struct fields are pub and independently mutable. Callers can set is_sent=true with is_validated=false, status="" or status="garbage", and sent_at_epoch_ms=None, creating multiple illegal states the compiler cannot prevent.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariants (e.g., sent budgets must be validated, must have a timestamp, must have a valid status) are enforced by convention not by the type system. Any crate user can corrupt budget lifecycle state without compilation errors.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Replace status: String with a typed enum (BudgetStatus: Draft, Validated, Sent). Replace is_validated/is_sent bools with the enum or a typestate. Require sent_at_epoch_ms at construction for Sent state. Provide a fallible constructor or builder that enforces invariants.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are separate primitive flags instead of a single typestate enum. This allows inconsistent combinations like (is_validated=false, is_sent=true) which represents a budget marked sent but never validated.
findings.failure_mode: Business logic that assumes sent budgets are validated will encounter runtime errors or silently process invalid budgets. The bool pair has 4 states but only 3 are valid (draft, validated, sent), making one illegal state representable.
findings.fix: Replace both bools with a single enum: pub enum BudgetStage { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. This makes invalid states unrepresentable at compile time and encodes the timestamp requirement into the Sent variant.

findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary values ("sent", "SENT", "", null-embedded, future unknown values). The mark_sent function sets status="sent" by string literal, which is fragile and unenforceable.
findings.failure_mode: Typos in status strings, case mismatches, or unknown status values break downstream logic at runtime. No exhaustive matching is possible on a String.
findings.fix: Replace with a sealed enum: pub enum BudgetStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent }. Use exhaustive match everywhere status is inspected.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership of the entire struct, mutates all fields inline, and returns the same struct. There is no validation gate — it transitions any state (including already-sent or invalid states) to sent without checking prerequisites like is_validated.
findings.failure_mode: A budget can be sent without validation, or sent multiple times. The function has no preconditions and cannot reject invalid transitions, violating the functional-core principle of pure, invariant-enforcing logic.
findings.fix: Replace with a fallible method or function: pub fn mark_sent(item: &BudgetWorkflow) -> Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError>. Validate is_validated is true, check status is not already Sent, then construct the new state with sent_at_epoch_ms set. Return a typed error for rejected transitions.

findings.problem: id: String is a free-form identifier with no validation, formatting, or newtype wrapping. The domain treats IDs as values with rules (format, uniqueness, lifetime) but the type provides no constraints.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, malformed IDs, or duplicate IDs are silently accepted. Downstream code must repeatedly validate the same invariant.
findings.fix: Introduce a typed newtype: pub struct BudgetId(String) with a fallible constructor BudgetId::new(s: &str) -> Result<Self, BudgetError> that validates format rules at the parse boundary.

findings.problem: All fields are pub, meaning any caller can mutate BudgetWorkflow fields directly without going through the domain API. This completely bypasses mark_sent and any future validation logic.
findings.failure_mode: External code can set item.is_sent = false after mark_sent runs, or set item.status = "" without any domain check, breaking all invariants in a single line of code.
findings.fix: Remove pub from all fields. Provide immutable accessors (pub fn id(&self), pub fn status(&self)) and a single public mutation path (mark_sent or a builder pattern) that enforces all invariants.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no error return type. It silently accepts invalid source states and overwrites them, providing no feedback to the caller about rejected transitions.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot detect or handle failed transitions. A budget sent without validation proceeds silently through the system, causing data integrity issues downstream.
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum: pub enum BudgetError { AlreadySent, NotValidated }. Change signature to pub fn mark_sent(item: &BudgetWorkflow) -> Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError> and return specific errors for rejected transitions.

residual_risk: The crate represents a fundamentally underspecified domain model: all state is externally mutable, no invariants are enforced by the type system, and mark_sent has no validation or error reporting. Every field combination is legal, making this code unsuitable for any production budget workflow. The structural issues require a full typestate redesign, not incremental fixes. No commands were executed; all findings are static review.
